messages.subject: legend.position="bottom"
parts:

linetype=factor(cut)))+geom_density()+opts(legend.position="bottom")
Error in grid.Call.graphics("L_setviewport", pvp, TRUE) :
Non-finite location and/or size for viewport

Similar problems for "left" and "top", although each produces its own
visual artefact... not really a graph.

Only legend.position="right" works AOK.

I had been using viewport earlier in the day, but this is from a new start.

messages.author: 3b0940ce7a895cd1
messages.subject: Re: legend.position="bottom"
parts:
Thanks Andreas,

What is remarkable is how much of ggplot works at this level in its development. (Hadley take a bow!).
I'll use GIMP to fix the problem.

For Hadley,  the problem I was trying to solve with moving the legend was wanting to have one legend across three plots which were brought together using viewport.  I really only wanted one legend, and would have been happiest if it was on the right, but then then two plots that did not have the legend grow longer, as compared with the third plot which does have the legend. I tried to move it to the bottom to reduce this, but I suspect now that ggplot would compress the vertical size of the bottom plot (with legend).

It occurs to me now that the judicious application of plyr might allow me to facet these data, and that will (I believe) solve this small problem.

Rob

yes if you have only some plots, gimp and even better inkscape (when
using svg) can resolve such problems really fast.

> For Hadley, the problem I was trying to solve with moving the legend was
> wanting to have one legend across three plots which were brought together
> using viewport. I really only wanted one legend, and would have been
> happiest if it was on the right, but then then two plots that did not have
> the legend grow longer, as compared with the third plot which does have the
> legend. I tried to move it to the bottom to reduce this, but I suspect now
> that ggplot would compress the vertical size of the bottom plot (with
> legend).

one solution for this would be to plot three plots without legend and one
plot which consists only of the legend and arrange them using viewport.

described in this example:
http://learnr.wordpress.com/2009/05/26/ggplot2-two-or-more-plots-sharing-the-same-legend/


regards,
stefan
